body:
## What this is

Drew, 2026-10-29: hunt for "jewels" — AI capabilities already available but not configured — as scheduled tasks, inside GitHub Actions, API/event-triggered, or as failure-triggered triage; plus verdicts on ChatGPT and Claude scheduled tasks. Study: ~/workspace/research_notes/unconfigured-jewels-20261029/findings.md.

Baseline (not an AI desert): Jules runs scheduled (daily ideation/flake-sync/upstream-sync) and as remediation (issue-label + PR-branch CI-failure-fix); a designed main-broken chain (#1779 §5) runs in all four repos (workflow_run → Breakage-ID dedupe → one issue → Jules first, ≤3 concurrent, 24h release → fleet queue); code's flake-inputs-update has a failure→Jules→Claude escalation ladder; OpenChamber has a bot suite (pr-review, help, summarize); opencode has a /review bot; opencode + openchamber now have consolidated LLM repo-sweepers (15-min triage/intake/duplicates). Trigger census across all workflow files: workflow_dispatch 54, schedule 23, workflow_run 5, **repository_dispatch 0**.

## The jewels, ranked by value ÷ effort

1. **Dependabot-alert triage agent.** Live counts: **code ≥100 open alerts (API page cap hit), opencode 33, openchamber 3, nix 0** — and nothing reads them. This is the fleet's largest untriaged queue, and it is the security queue. Design: scout-tier scheduled pass on the repo-sweeper chassis — group by ecosystem/severity/reachability, dismiss dev-only/unreachable WITH recorded reasons, one grouped fix issue per cluster, criticals escalated same-day.
2. **Classifier leg on the main-broken chain + coverage for the other "right kinds."** The chain files and routes well, but nobody reads a failure before Jules/queue spend — and most failures are knowable classes (runner stalls, missing-secret, flakes). Uncovered by construction today: release workflows (goreleaser/Release/publish file nothing), the automation's own workflows (openchamber's repo sweeper failed repeatedly today, unwatched; nix's buffer-backup lock sync likewise), PR-tier failures. Design in the failure-triage section below.
3. **Jules API as a first-class queue executor.** The fleet uses only the jules-action wrapper; the REST API (v1alpha: sessions, activity polling, sendMessage, approvePlan) makes Jules the **only vendor agent Muse can both dispatch AND poll** — it fits the Supabase queue with the same outcome/time review fields as OpenCode/OpenClaw. **BUG: opencode has no JULES_API_KEY secret, so its Jules-first leg cannot fire** (noted in its own main-broken.yml header). Close that gap first.
4. **repository_dispatch bridge (zero today).** The outbound twin of #2072's inbound webhook hot list: fleet/Worker/Supabase events starting GitHub-side agent runs without a laptop runner, replacing several pollers with events.
5. **Port the repo-sweeper to code and nix.** Those two repos still get first-look triage from Claude-side cron sweeps — exactly the "Muse task launching OpenCode" spend Drew wants cut (see #2174). Includes label-only stale handling (Drew's rule; only openchamber has it).
6. **Small ones:** PR-branch failure classifier, comment-only (≥3 same Breakage-ID in 24h → one classification comment; no fix attempts, no Jules budget); code is the only repo with no /oc mention bot; Copilot cloud agent workflows exist in all four repos but seat/usage is unverified — a 10-minute check before counting it as an executor.

## Failure-triage design (the "right kind", scoped narrowly)

In scope: main-tier failures (already chained), release/publish failures, automation-own workflows, repeated PR-tier failures. Never: single PR failures, cancels, experiment branches. Pipeline: the existing deterministic shell step computes the Breakage-ID and dedupes → a NEW scout step (`opencode run` on the repo key, same in-Actions pattern as the sweepers) reads the failing jobs' log tails and classifies: infra-runner / infra-network / quota-or-secret / flake-suspect / real-regression / unknown — attaching 3–5 evidence log lines to the issue as an agent-note:v1 comment BEFORE any fix spend. Routing: quota/secret → immediate escalation to Drew with the exact fix named, zero fix attempts; infra → one automatic re-run of failed jobs, repeat escalates as infrastructure (when Actions itself is stalled, in-Actions triage cannot run — the external fleet-watchdog stays the backstop, and the classifier says "infrastructure" rather than filing code fixes); flake → one re-run, green closes as flake with a strike counter, third strike files a flake-fix issue; real regression → existing Jules-budget/queue routing with the diagnosis attached. Authority limits: the agent may re-run failed jobs once per breakage, comment/label/file within chain labels, dispatch Jules within budget; it may NOT edit code, merge, touch secrets, or disable workflows — anything else is an "escalating:" comment + status/needs-triage. Every step lands as an agent-note so outcome/time/tokens audit into the same review table as the OpenCode/OpenClaw comparison (#2072). Preserve the chain's guardrails: no workflow_run on "*" (#304), per-breakage concurrency, dry-run mode.

## ChatGPT scheduled tasks — verdict: usable niche, fire-and-forget

Relaunched June 2026 (dedicated Scheduled page): one-off/recurring/monitoring tasks, at most hourly, web search + connected apps; event triggers via Gmail/Slack/GitHub on paid plans. Limits by tier: 3 active (Go) / 5 (Plus) / 10 (Business, Edu) / 15 (Pro, Enterprise). Caveats: **Tasks cannot run GPTs** — a Task is generic ChatGPT, not Aster (no persona/memory): a separate, dumber-but-unattended executor. **"ProLite" appears in no published tier table** — Drew's task allowance is unverified until checked on his Scheduled page. Fits only off-fleet monitoring (vendor status/changelog watches, Gmail-event nudges, public-web digests). Monitoring gap: **no API exists to create, list, or audit tasks or runs** — Muse cannot confirm one is alive, and unattended tasks can silently auto-pause. Convention: every task's instructions end with "email the full result to drewrypope@gmail.com, subject [CHATGPT-TASK <name>]" (Muse reads Gmail) or post via the Slack app to a channel Muse reads; the weekly ChatGPT export (#2072) is the retrospective audit; a Claude-side registry treats a missed cadence as presumed-dead and surfaces it. Residual risk: silence is the only failure signal.

## Claude scheduled tasks — verdict: blocked, and a poor fit anyway

All three surfaces (Claude Code Routines — cloud, schedule/API/GitHub-webhook triggers, caps Pro 5 / Max 15 / Team+Ent 25 runs/day, 1-hour minimum interval; Desktop scheduled tasks — app must be open; Cowork scheduled tasks) require a paid claude.ai plan; **Drew's claude.ai is on the free tier**, so the surfaces do not even appear. Even unblocked, the fit is poor: Routines' API trigger is fire-only (returns a session URL; no endpoint reads a result, sends follow-up, or cancels; no idempotency key). The one additive surface (laptop-closed pure-repo work) is already covered by Jules free tier + Actions. **Do not buy a seat for this.** (Distinct pots: Drew's free claude.ai ≠ the assistant's own Muse subscription ≠ the Meta Muse API pool.) If ever used, monitoring is the same self-reporting-output convention as ChatGPT Tasks.

## Worth-it measurement (Drew, 2026-10-29 — applies to every executor surface)

Each surface gets measured per task class against doing the work via OpenCode or Muse directly: outcome quality, Muse supervision minutes, allowance burn (exact tokens where metered; plan-level % delta where not). A class that is not worth it is a finding, not a failure. Companion agents (Aster today; a Claude equivalent later) are additionally valued as chat partners and escalation points independent of task volume, and their task mechanics (what triggers a billable work job vs plain chat, rough work-job cost, effort levels) get learned empirically and recorded. Cross-cutting fact from the study: of every vendor surface examined, only the Jules API gives Muse both dispatch and result polling; ChatGPT Tasks and Claude Routines are fire-and-forget from Muse's seat.

## Acceptance

- Dependabot triage pass running with its first grouped report (all four repos).
- opencode JULES_API_KEY gap closed (or escalated with the reason recorded).
- Classifier leg implemented on the main-broken chain in one repo, dry-run first, with the routing rules above.
- ChatGPT Scheduled-page allowance for Drew's plan verified and recorded here.
